title: CRLR/28/2013 of RAJNI ALIAS MEENAKSHI Vs NAR SINGH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 28 of 2013
Rajni @ Meenakshi ...Revisionist
Vs.
Nar Singh ...Respondent
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate for the revisionist.
None appears for the respondent.
With
Criminal Revision No. 289 of 2013
Nar Singh ...Revisionist
Vs.
Rajni @ Meenakshi ...Respondent
None appears for the revisionist.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate for the respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
 In the present Criminal Revision No. 28 of 2013 'Rajni
@ Meenakshi vs. Nar Singh' the revisionist (wife), has challenged
the judgment dated 23.11.2012 as rendered by the Judge, Family
Court, Haridwar, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 145 of 2007
'Smt. Rajni @ Meenakshi vs. Nar Singh', whereby, in the
proceedings, which were held under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. the
Family Court has determined the maintenance payable to the
revisionist, only at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month. As far as the
maintenance claimed for the applicant nos. 2 and 3, i.e. the minor
daughters, is concerned, the maintenance has been declined by the
Family Court. In the connected criminal revision being Criminal
Revision No. 289 of 2012 'Nar Singh vs. Rajni @ Meenakshi' the
husband has put a challenge to the impugned judgment dated
23.11.2012, wherein, a determination of maintenance, which has been
directed to be made payable at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month from
the date of the order has been put to challenge by the revisionist
(husband). In the two connected revisions following reliefs were
sought:
"(a) Criminal Revision No. 28 of 2013- This criminal
revision is being preferred against the judgment and order
dated 23.11.2012 passed by Mr. Pradeep Pant, Family Judge,

2
Haridwar, in Criminal Misc. Case no. 145/2007 Smt. Rajni @
Meenakshi vs. Nar Singh, for enhancing the amount granted
by allowing the application of the revisionist against the
respondent under section 125 of Cr.P.C.
(b) Criminal Revision No. 289 of 2013- This criminal
revision against the judgment and order dated 23.11.2012
passed by Judge Family Court Haridwar in Criminal Case No.
145 of 2007 Smt. Rajni Alias Meenakshi and Others vs. Nar
Singh awarding the maintenance to opposite to the tune of Rs.
10,000/- per month from the date of moving application under
Section 125 Cr.P.C.".
2. List revised. None has appeared for the revisionist of
Criminal Revision No. 289 of 2012. In the Criminal Revision No. 28
of 2013 the notices were issued to the respondent (husband) and there
is an office report of Registry dated 31.07.2018 that as per the process
server report the respondent (husband) had been served personally on
20.04.2013, but yet he has not put in appearance in the present
Criminal Revision No. 28 of 2013. Even in the connected revision
where the husband has challenged the impugned order, none had
appeared to assist the court on its own merit even in the revised call.
Hence, the court proceeds to adjudicate the criminal revisions on its
own merit.
3. The facts, which emerges for consideration is that the fact
of matrimony having been solemnized between the revisionist (wife)
1 and the respondent (husband) about six years prior to the institution
of the proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. is a fact, which has
not been disputed and is rather admitted inter se between the parties.
Another fact, which stands admitted is that out of the said matrimony
two daughters Ishika and Akriti, were born and who at the time of
institution of the proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. were about
5 and 3 years of age respectively.
4. The case of the revisionist (wife) before the court below
in her 125 Cr.P.C application was that there were atrocities exercised
upon her by the in-laws of hers; on account of being dissatisfied with
the quantum of dowry, which she has brought from her parents as a
consequence of the marriage held between the revisionist (wife) and

3
the respondent (husband) herein. Being dissatisfied with the amount
of dowry her case was that she was maltreated and on 26.01.2007, she
was physically assaulted and she was thrown out from the
matrimonial home along with her two minor daughters and ever since
then her case is that she is residing with her parent, though her case in
the application under Section 125 Cr.P.C., is that several efforts were
made by her parents to get the dispute resolved, but no heed was paid
towards it, but rather the respondent (husband) had further aggravated
his atrocities as against the present revisionist (wife) and thus she
contends that since she is not having any independent source of
earning, coupled with the fact since the respondent (husband) is
earning about Rs. 10,000/- per month being engaged in the business of
mobile repairing and has got his agricultural land and, hence, it is
projected by her that he is having an income of about Rs. 30,000/- per
month and, hence, she has claimed that she may be awarded a
maintenance at the rate of Rs. 5,000/- per month and for minor
daughters she has claimed that maintenance be determined at the rate
of Rs. 3,000/- each may be granted to the daughters.
5. The said application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. of the
wife was opposed by the respondent (husband) by filing an objection
paper no. 9C denying the theory of atrocities as well as the allegation
levelled by her that she was maltreated by the in-laws on the pretext
of being dissatisfied with the dowry, which the parents of the
revisionist (wife) has provided and the respondent (husband), in his
objection had also denied that the manner in which the income, which
was accruing to him has been projected by the revisionist (wife) in her
application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., it is the figures, which are
contrary to the records because he has submitted that he has got no
permanent shop as such from where he is conducting the so called
business of mobile repairing, nor any such independent witness has
been produced by the wife on record to show and establish that he was
having an income of Rs. 30,000/- as pleaded in the application, which
was filed by her under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

4
6. On the contrary, the pleading taken by the respondent
(husband) in defense was that he is engaged as a labourer and has got
an income of about Rs. 1,800/- per month only while on the other
hand, though without there being any evidence, he has submitted that
the revisionist (wife) is having her independent income from the
tuitions, which she is conducting and thus she is having an income of
about Rs. 7,000/- per month and, hence, she is not entitled for being
paid any maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C. because there is no
dearth of income with her and she could easily maintain herself.
7. The revisionist (wife) in support of her contention apart
from producing herself in witness box PW1, has also produced in
witness one Mr. Yashpal Singh as PW2, who had examined himself in
support of the application and apart from it she has also placed on
record the documents and the other proceedings, which was held inter
se amongst themselves being Miscellaneous Case No. 35 of 2007 as
paper no. 19/2 to 19/4, in which there was an order passed on
19.10.2007, which showed the conditions under which the
controversy between the revisionist and respondent had arisen.
8. On the other hand, the respondent (husband) apart from
producing certain medical documents paper no. 29/1 to 29/32 with
regards to the treatment of the minor children, which has been
undertaken by him. He had also placed reliance on the proceedings of
Miscellaneous Case No. 757 of 2010. In order to substantiate that as
far as the act of desertion is concerned, that is at the behest of the
revisionist (wife) and since she is voluntarily residing away from her
matrimonial home since 26.01.2007 she would not be entitled for
grant of any maintenance in view of the provisions contained under
Section 125(4) because she had declined to discharge her matrimonial
obligation, and is living separately for no valid reasons.
9. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the learned Family
Court after having considered the rival impact of pleading and
evidence with regards to the effect of the proceedings under Section

5
498A of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, which was
registered as Case No. 861 of 2011, and various other judicial
proceedings, which was held inter se amongst themselves, the Family
Court has recorded a finding that in view of paper no. 29 ka 1, which
was an application paper no. 117/27, the report of the recounselling
committee and its report paper no. 29ka/38 to 29ka/ 39 thereof, which
showed that as amongst the parties to the proceedings of Section 125
Cr.P.C. there is no such incident was ever established by evidence
beyond doubt with regards to the demand of dowry. But however
looking to the atrocities and the complaint, which has been registered
by the revisionist (wife) before the police authorities, the Family
Court has recorded a finding that revisionist (wife) has got all valid
and justified reason to reside separately from the respondent
(husband) and as such the bar of determining the maintenance as
contemplated under sub-section (4) of Section 125 of Cr.P.C will not
come into play in the circumstances of the present case. Consequently,
the learned Family Court even otherwise also while dealing with the
amount of income accruing to the respondent (husband) has not
recorded any specific finding as to what was the actual income
accruing to the respondent (husband) and by recording the finding to
the effect that it was not substantiated by any evidence or on
consideration of any document the pleading raised by the respondent
the Family Court by the impugned judgment dated 23.11.2012 had
determined the maintenance as directed to be made payable to the
revisionist (wife) at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month to the revisionist
(wife), but as far as the maintenance to applicant nos. 2 and 3, i.e. the
minor daughters, are concerned, the same was denied by the Family
Court.
10. The plea taken by the respondent (husband) with regards
to his source of income was not substantiated or proved by him on
record before the court below to the effect that it was on a lower side
as claimed by him and, hence, the Family Court while considering the
case of the revisionist (wife) pertaining to the income accruing to the
respondent (husband) at the rate of Rs. 30,000/- per month has drawn
an inference to the contrary because of the fact that the existence of

6
any permanent establishment by way of shop in which the business
was allegedly being conducted by him was not proved by the
revisionist (wife) in order to show that her husband was profitably
engaged, but yet the learned Family Court by the impugned judgment
dated 23.11.2012 has also simultaneously not recorded any plausible
reasoning with regards to the defense taken by the respondent
(husband) pertaining to his engagement as a labourer and the income
accruing to him as to be too meager, because under law of evidence
once the husband has taken a plea in defense that he was a labourer
and he was having no source of income then it was rather his
responsibility, which was casted upon him to be discharged by him in
the proceedings before the court below in order to show as to what
was the actual income accruing to him, contrary to what has been
pleaded by the revisionist (wife) in her application under Section 125
of Cr.P.C. This responsibility was not discharged by the respondent
(husband) to prove that he was not having the income as pleaded by
the revisionist (wife) for determining the quantum of maintenance.
11. In the absence of there being any finding to the contrary
pertaining to the rival contentions with regards to the income accruing
to the respondent (husband) the amount of maintenance as determined
at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month is without any plausible reasoning
assigned by the Family Court below and, consequently, the said
determination of maintenance is held to be too meager and even
otherwise also quite logically in the present era of inflation it is
practically impossible for the revisionist (wife), who is not having any
independent source of earning nor proved to be having any income, to
sustain herself and to meet her bare necessities on the amount of
maintenance as determined at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month. Even
otherwise the determination made was not correlated with the actual
income, which was accruing to the respondent (husband).
12. Hence, this Court holds the said determination of
maintenance at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month as to be without an
application of mind contrary to the evidence on record and without
even assigning any logical reason as to what parameters were adopted

7
by the Family Court to determine and conclude that Rs. 1,000/- would
be a proper amount of maintenance to be made payable to the
revisionist (wife). Hence, it is being held that it is too meager amount
contrary to the evidence and rather based upon misappreciation of
evidence, which required an enhancement.
13. While considering the aspect as to what would be the
appropriate and adequate maintenance payable to the revisionist
(wife) by means of which she would be able to reasonably maintain
herself, the maintenance herein contemplated under Section 125 of
Cr.P.C. contemplates that it ought to be a maintenance, which
otherwise the revisionist (wife) would have been entitled to have
enjoyed had the matrimony between the revisionist (wife) and the
respondent (husband) subsisted without there being any matrimonial
discord amongst themselves.
14. The ratio propounded by the Hon'ble Apex Court in
various precedents it has normally laid down that the wife in her
proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C. would be entitled for 1/3rd of
the amount of income accruing to her husband, to be paid to her by
way of maintenance, the said amount of 1/3rd of husband's income has
been determined to be reasonable amount, which revisionist (wife)
would be normally entitled to receive for bare maintenance. The said
aspect has not been dealt with by the learned Family Court, while
passing the impugned judgment dated 23.11.2012. Even the Family
Court has not dealt with the aspect that the revisionist (wife) is
entitled to maintain her stature of living equivalent to that of her
husband, which she would otherwise have been entitled to enjoy had
there not been any matrimonial discord amongst themselves.
15. Consequently, holding that the amount as determined by
the Family Court by the impugned judgment is too meager, the said
amount is accordingly directed to be enhanced to be paid at the rate of
Rs. 3,000/- and the same is directed to be made payable from the date
of the application itself. The arrears of the said period is directed to be

8
remitted by the respondent (husband) within a period of two months
from the date of production of certified copy of this judgment before
the Family Court, Haridwar. As far as the amount as enhanced
towards maintenance at the rate of Rs. 3,000/-, the same is directed to
be paid by the respondent (husband) to the revisionist (wife) by 10th of
each month.
16. Since having held that the determination of maintenance
at the rate of Rs. 1,000/- per month by the impugned judgment dated
23.11.2012 was too meager and without proper appreciation of
evidence, and contrary to the evidence on record and since it was
based upon misappreciation of the evidence on record by the court
below, the criminal revision preferred by the husband being Criminal
Revision No. 289 of 2012 in view of enhancement made in criminal
revision of wife would stand dismissed. Even otherwise also, since
none has appeared to assist the court no interference is called for in
the said revision preferred by the respondent (husband). Accordingly,
the Revision No. 28 of 2013 'Rajni @ Meenakshi vs. Nar Singh',
which has been preferred by the revisionist (wife) is partly allowed.
As far as the Criminal Revision No. 289 of 2012 'Nar Singh vs. Rajni
@ Meenakshi' is devoid of any merit and the same is, accordingly,
dismissed.
17. Let the copy of this judgment be placed on the records of
Criminal Revision No. 289 of 2012 'Nar Singh vs. Rajni @
Meenakshi'.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 09.01.2020
Pooja
